brief.headline: The aluminium price on this page is still Friday's - the London exchange has not set a new one yet today - but the two things that sit underneath it have both turned against the metal since yesterday: talks on reopening Gulf shipping were called off, and Saudi Arabia shut the 7-million-barrel-a-day pipeline that was the main way of getting oil out without using the Gulf, sending oil to a four-month high and European gas up nearly 5%.
bullets: THE PRICE ON THIS PAGE IS FRIDAY'S, AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING TO SAY. This report compiles just after four in the morning London time and the exchange does not set today's official price until 1:20 in the afternoon, so the figures here are still Friday 11-September: aluminium at $3,274 a tonne for metal you take now and $3,250 for metal in three months. Friday's fall of about two percent was caused by American inflation figures, not by anything to do with aluminium - every metal on the exchange fell the same day.

YESTERDAY'S GOOD NEWS ON THE GULF HAS BEEN WITHDRAWN, AND THIS PAGE IS SAYING SO RATHER THAN QUIETLY MOVING ON. On Saturday and Sunday this report carried Iran's statement that a deal with Oman on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was days away. That meeting has now been POSTPONED, announced by Oman's own foreign minister, with Saudi Arabia reported to have concerns about the proposal and Bahrain saying it will not take part. Nothing has got physically worse in the water, but the path out of the problem just got longer.

ENERGY WENT THE OPPOSITE WAY TO YESTERDAY, AND ENERGY IS THE BIGGEST SINGLE COST OF MAKING ALUMINIUM. Oil rose about 3% to nearly $108 a barrel, a four-month high, and European gas rose about 4.6% to roughly EUR 83 a megawatt hour. The reason is specific: Saudi Arabia has shut its East-West pipeline after drone attacks on Thursday, with no date for restarting it. That pipeline carries around 7 million barrels a day to the Red Sea and was the main route AROUND the Gulf chokepoint - so losing it puts the risk back onto the waterway everyone is arguing about.

THE ONE ENCOURAGING SIGN FROM FRIDAY IS STILL STANDING BUT STILL UNTESTED. Metal for immediate delivery remains $24 a tonne dearer than metal in three months, and that gap barely moved when the price fell sharply - usually a sign that real buyers are short of metal. It has now gone four days without a test. WHAT TO WATCH: today's exchange price at 1:20pm London and whether that $24 premium survives, then the US Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision on Wednesday 16 September - and note that oil's rise is happening while the world's energy agencies are cutting their forecasts for how much oil will be needed, which makes this cost increase less solid than it looks.

Yesterday this page lowered its geopolitical risk trend on the 07-September report that a deal was days away; that decision is reversed today. SECOND, THE BYPASS IS DOWN: Saudi Arabia has suspended its East-West crude pipeline after Thursday's drone attacks with no restart date, roughly 7 million barrels a day of capacity to Red Sea ports and the principal route AROUND the strait. THAT IS THE COST FLOOR RISING AT THE SAME TIME AS THE DOLLAR - DXY 99.33, +0.21%, WITH THE FEDERAL RESERVE TWO DAYS AWAY AND THE SAME PUBLISHER'S OWN HEADLINE READING THAT COPPER IS EXTENDING ITS FALL ON HAWKISH FED BETS. DEARER POWER WITH A FIRMER DOLLAR IS THE WORST OF THE FOUR COMBINATIONS: IT SQUEEZES THE MARGIN AND CAPS THE PRICE AT ONCE. THE COUNTERWEIGHT IS KEPT VISIBLE BECAUSE IT IS REAL AND BECAUSE IT IS WHAT THE SPIKE WOULD FALL BACK INTO: the IEA has cut 2026 global oil demand by 2.5 million barrels a day, the largest annual contraction since the pandemic, OPEC has cut its demand-growth forecast for a fifth consecutive time, and the EIA has raised its 2027 US production forecast to 14.3 million b/d. SO THE HONEST SUMMARY IS THAT THE COST BASE SPLIT IN TWO OVERNIGHT: POWER AND FREIGHT RISK UP, ORE AND ALUMINA STILL LOOSE. The next published official is today at 13:20 London; the Federal Reserve decides on 16-September.

drivers.text: THE GULF-SCARCITY PILLAR UNDER EVERY WESTERN PREMIUM ON THIS PANEL WEAKENED AGAIN, AND THIS TIME THE EVIDENCE IS DIPLOMATIC RATHER THAN COMMERCIAL — Regional premiums outside China are underwritten by two assumptions: that Gulf metal is scarce, and that Gulf routes are unreliable. BOTH WERE CONTRADICTED THIS WEEK BY DIFFERENT SOURCES. On the commercial side, an 11-September market review states that outside China production resumptions and new ramp-ups continued, that DAMAGED CAPACITY IN THE MIDDLE EAST RECOVERED, and that supply outside China kept repairing. On the routing side, dated reporting of 07-September has Iran saying an agreement with Oman to manage Strait of Hormuz shipping is days away, with a temporary route already agreed in late August. logistics.note: THIS ROW IS RAISED BACK FROM IMPAIRED-BUT-DE-ESCALATING TO IMPAIRED-WITH-NO-DATED-PATH-OUT, REVERSING YESTERDAY'S DOWNGRADE, AND THE REVERSAL IS SET OUT IN FULL BECAUSE THIS JUDGEMENT MOVED TWICE IN 48 HOURS. Reporting attributes the delay to Saudi concerns over the proposal, and Bahrain has said it would not participate. The United States and Iran remain at an impasse over control of the waterway. THE 07-SEPTEMBER REPORTING THAT IRAN DESCRIBED A DEAL AS DAYS AWAY IS NOT DELETED AND WAS NOT WRONG - IT IS SUPERSEDED BY THE FACT THAT THE MEETING IT POINTED TO DID NOT HAPPEN. AND THE BYPASS IS NOW DOWN, WHICH IS THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF OF TODAY'S CHANGE: Saudi Arabia has suspended its East-West crude pipeline after Thursday's drone attacks with no restart date - around 7 million barrels a day of capacity to Red Sea ports and the principal route that routes AROUND this strait. A CHOKEPOINT WITHOUT A WORKING BYPASS IS A DIFFERENT RISK FROM A CHOKEPOINT WITH ONE. THE WATERWAY HAS NOT REOPENED, NOTHING HAS BEEN SIGNED, AND NO NEW MEETING DATE HAS BEEN PUBLISHED. Brent at a four-month high is the market's own vote on this row.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: A SECOND CHOKEPOINT REMAINS IN PLAY AND NOTHING PUBLISHED THIS WEEKEND CHANGED IT. The Houthi group was reported to have seized the port city of Mocha, gaining leverage over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, declaring a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia and striking Saudi energy infrastructure; Bab el-Mandeb transits are down about 24% since the July blockade and MARAD advisory 2026-006 runs to 22-September. THE IMPORTANCE IS ROUTING RATHER THAN VOLUME: Bab el-Mandeb is the alternative on which Hormuz-affected cargo has partly relied, so two contested chokepoints are not twice the risk of one - THEY REMOVE THE SUBSTITUTE. THAT LOGIC NOW RUNS IN REVERSE AND IT IS WORTH SAYING SO: if the Hormuz arrangement reported on 07-September completes, the pressure on Bab el-Mandeb as a substitute route falls at the same time, and the shipping-risk premium embedded in Western delivered prices unwinds from both ends at once. headlines.title: TALKS BETWEEN IRAN AND GULF STATES ON A TEMPORARY STRAIT OF HORMUZ SHIPPING CORRIDOR HAVE BEEN POSTPONED, STATED PUBLICLY BY OMAN'S FOREIGN MINISTER BADR ALBUSAIDI, WITH SAUDI CONCERNS OVER THE PROPOSAL REPORTED AND BAHRAIN DECLINING TO PARTICIPATE. The United States and Iran remain at an impasse over control of the waterway. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL ITEM ON THE PAGE TODAY BECAUSE IT REVERSES THE DIRECTION THIS PAGE CARRIED YESTERDAY. On 13-September this page upgraded the Iran-Oman arrangement to dated multi-outlet reporting and lowered the geopolitical risk trend on it; the 07-September report was accurate as reported, but the meeting it pointed to did not happen. THE PHYSICAL SITUATION HAS NOT WORSENED - NO NEW CLOSURE, NO NEW STRIKE ON A SMELTER - WHAT HAS WORSENED IS THE PATH OUT, AND FOR A MARKET THAT PRICES A CHOKEPOINT PREMIUM MONTHS FORWARD, THE PATH OUT IS THE PRICE.

SAUDI ARABIA HAS SUSPENDED OPERATIONS ON ITS EAST-WEST CRUDE PIPELINE AFTER THURSDAY'S DRONE ATTACKS, WITH NO INDICATION YET OF WHEN IT RESUMES. The line carries crude across Saudi Arabia to Red Sea ports with capacity of around 7 million barrels a day AND IS THE PRINCIPAL ROUTE USED TO BYPASS THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ. THE SIGNIFICANCE IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN NUMERICAL: the bypass was the physical hedge against the chokepoint, so its loss concentrates regional export risk back onto the waterway that is itself contested, at the same moment the diplomatic route to reopening that waterway has been postponed. Brent rose toward $108 a barrel, a four-month high, on this item, after gaining more than 9% last week. FOR AN ALUMINIUM READER THIS IS BOTH AN ENERGY-COST ITEM AND A FREIGHT-RISK ITEM AT ONCE, WHICH IS WHY IT SITS AT THE TOP OF THIS LIST RATHER THAN IN THE MACRO PANEL ALONE.

THE INTERNATIONAL ENERGY AGENCY HAS SHARPLY CUT ITS OUTLOOK FOR GLOBAL OIL DEMAND, FORECASTING A 2.5 MILLION-BARREL-A-DAY CONTRACTION IN 2026 - THE LARGEST ANNUAL DECLINE SINCE THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC - AND WARNED DEMAND COULD WEAKEN FURTHER IF THE CONFLICT PERSISTS. OPEC has cut its 2026 demand-growth forecast for a fifth consecutive time and the EIA has raised its 2027 US crude production forecast to 14.3 million barrels a day. THIS IS THE REASON TODAY'S ENERGY SPIKE IS NOT TREATED AS A DURABLE COST FLOOR. A supply-route closure lifts the price of the barrel without changing how many barrels the world wants, and the forecasts for how many barrels the world wants are being cut aggressively. IF THE PIPELINE RESTARTS, THIS ROW IS WHAT THE PRICE FALLS BACK INTO.

A DATED 12-SEPTEMBER SMM WEEKLY REVIEW CARRIED BY AL CIRCLE READS THAT CHINA CONTINUES DESTOCKING WITH RECOVERING PEAK-SEASON DEMAND AND EXPECTS ALUMINIUM PRICES TO CONSOLIDATE AT HIGHS WITH AN UPWARD BIAS. Its own macro framing cites the 09-September Revolutionary Guard strikes on tankers and merchant vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and Brent breaking $100 to close at $101.21. THE EVIDENTIAL WEIGHT IS CAPPED AND THE CAP IS STATED: this is commentary carrying a directional view rather than a measured balance or a disclosed inventory figure. It is included because it is the only dated Chinese physical read available this morning and because it points the OPPOSITE way to the bearish upstream volume block this page carried over the weekend - a disagreement worth showing rather than resolving.

THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION HAS DELAYED ITS PLANNED MEASURES ON ALUMINIUM SCRAP EXPORTS, REPLACING THE EARLIER PROPOSAL FOR EXPORT DUTIES WITH RESTRICTIONS ON WASTE SHIPMENTS TO NON-OECD COUNTRIES, per dated 12-September reporting. European Aluminium has said the change added to discomfort across an industry that had been pressing for retention measures. THE DIRECTION OF THE SUBSTITUTION IS THE POINT FOR A FEEDSTOCK READER: an export duty raises the cost of shipping scrap out of Europe regardless of destination, while a non-OECD shipment restriction leaves OECD destinations open, so the measure as now framed retains European scrap less effectively than the proposal it replaced. THIS IS A EUROPEAN RECYCLED-METAL FEEDSTOCK ITEM AND IT IS NOT PRESENTED AS A PRIMARY-MARKET ITEM.

BAUXITE SUPPLY IS RISING AND FORWARD PRICE FORECASTS HAVE BEEN CUT ON BOTH MAJOR ORIGINS, PER THE DATED 12-SEPTEMBER ANALYSIS, AND THE BLOCK IS CARRIED UNCHANGED BECAUSE NOTHING NEWER HAS PRINTED AND NOTHING HAS CONTRADICTED IT. Guinean shipments were 4.33 Mt in the 21-27 August week, up 3.7% week on week and 28.4% year on year, even as some suspended Guinean mines continued to stockpile at port rather than resume shipping. Guinea FOB is forecast at $34-46/dmt for 2026 against $40-65/dmt in 2025; Australian FOB at $39.15/wmt in FY26 against $51.48/wmt in FY25. BECAUSE FOUR TO SIX TONNES OF BAUXITE STAND BEHIND EVERY TONNE OF METAL, THIS IS A MARGIN TAILWIND AND A PRICE HEADWIND - AND IT IS A DIFFERENT INPUT FROM THE POWER COST THAT ROSE TODAY, SO THE TWO ARE NOT NETTED AGAINST EACH OTHER HERE.

ASIA EXPORTED 7.05 Mt OF ALUMINA WORTH USD 2.76bn IN H1-2026, UP 27.36% YEAR ON YEAR, AND INDIA'S ALUMINA TRADE SURPLUS REACHED 1.72 Mt, NEARLY QUADRUPLE A YEAR EARLIER, WITH EXPORTS UP 51.3% TO 2.5 Mt AND IMPORTS DOWN 34.9% TO 775,362 t. Carried unchanged from the dated 12-September analysis. THE TEST THIS PAGE SET FOR ITSELF IS STILL OUTSTANDING AND IS RESTATED RATHER THAN DROPPED: the most recent dated alumina trade, 50,000 mt at $353.50/mt FOB East Australia on 11-September, was essentially flat on a five-week-old mark. TONNES MOVING WITHOUT PRICES MOVING IS WHAT SURPLUS LOOKS LIKE - BUT IF THE NEXT DATED TRADE IS ALSO FLAT RATHER THAN LOWER, THE SURPLUS IS BEING ABSORBED AND THE FALLING-COST READ IS WEAKER THAN THE VOLUME DATA SUGGESTS.

THE JAPANESE Q4 PRODUCER OFFER OF USD 310-325/t FOR OCTOBER-DECEMBER SHIPMENTS, DOWN 18-22% ON THE USD 395/t Q3 SETTLEMENT, WAS RESTATED BY A SECOND PUBLISHER ON 12-SEPTEMBER AND IS CARRIED UNCHANGED. The pending range on this page stays USD 280-310 and is NOT tightened, because corroboration of an existing reading is not a new mark and a range is not narrowed on repetition. THE NEWEST CONSENSUS OF USD 280-290 SITS BELOW THE PRODUCERS' OWN OFFER FLOOR, SO THE BURDEN OF CONCESSION IS ON THE SELLERS. A settlement at USD 285 would be a fall of roughly 28% in a single quarter.

THE SUPPLY RESPONSE TO THE HIGH-PRICE REGIME IS VISIBLE, DATED AND LATE BY DESIGN, AND THE LIST IS CARRIED UNCHANGED: NALCO has licensed EGA's DX+ Ultra technology for a proposed 500,000 t/y Angul expansion; Rio Tinto is acquiring the undeveloped Aurukun bauxite project from Glencore and Mitsubishi at potentially up to 8 Mdt/y; Rusal is planning an Indonesian bauxite-alumina complex; Ashapura is targeting 15 Mt/y of Guinean bauxite by FY28. NONE OF IT ADDS A TONNE IN 2026, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE HORIZON THE FORWARD CURVE ACTUALLY COVERS RATHER THAN FOR THIS QUARTER'S BALANCE.

THE US DEPARTMENT OF WAR HAS COMMITTED A FURTHER USD 100 MILLION TO THE ATLANTIC ALUMINA COMPANY, TAKING TOTAL GOVERNMENT INVESTMENT TO USD 400 MILLION, EXPLICITLY TO PROTECT THE COUNTRY'S LAST REMAINING DOMESTIC ALUMINA REFINERY AS A DEFENCE SUPPLY CHAIN. Carried unchanged from the dated 12-September analysis. STATE CAPITAL ENTERING A MARKET THAT THE VOLUME DATA SAYS IS IN SURPLUS IS A STATEMENT THAT THE SURPLUS IS NOT TRUSTED TO PERSIST, and it is the clearest single piece of evidence on this page that policy rather than price is now setting Western alumina capacity decisions.

CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS HAVE BEEN IN FORCE SINCE 08-SEPTEMBER AT 50% ACROSS USD 27.6bn OF IMPORTS AND MORE THAN 300 METALS PRODUCTS, AND THE ESCALATION CONTINUED ON 12-SEPTEMBER: Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs on approximately USD 20bn of US goods and the United States responded with a 50% tariff on about 100 categories of Canadian products FROM 15-SEPTEMBER - TOMORROW - plus a ban on certain Canadian motor vehicles and dairy products from 29-SEPTEMBER. WHETHER ALUMINIUM SITS INSIDE THOSE 100 CATEGORIES IS NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED IN THE SOURCE AND IS NOT ASSUMED HERE. US Section 232 is re-verified unchanged at 50% on articles and 25% on derivatives, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU.

THE STRUCTURAL SIGNAL FROM FRIDAY IS CARRIED UNCHANGED AND IS EXPLICITLY NOT UPGRADED. Flat price fell 2.06% and the cash-to-three-month backwardation gave up exactly one dollar, from USD 25.00 to USD 24.00, while warehouse stock drew for a fifth consecutive session. A FRAGILE FRONT-MONTH SIGNAL FLATTENS OR FLIPS UNDER A TWO-PERCENT SELL-OFF; THIS ONE DID NEITHER, WHICH SAYS THE SELL-OFF WAS FINANCIAL AND THE PHYSICAL MARKET DID NOT RATIFY IT. THE QUALIFICATION IS THAT IT HAS NOW GONE FOUR CALENDAR DAYS WITHOUT A TEST, AND AN UNTESTED SIGNAL IS NOT A STRONGER ONE. Today's 13:20 London official is the test.

Unaudited H1-2026 interim results, approved at an 18-August board meeting and filed 19-August: ADJUSTED EBITDA UP 64.4% TO US$1.23bn from US$748m; revenue up 10.9% to US$8.338bn from US$7.52bn; adjusted net profit US$196m against a US$194m loss a year earlier. earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY WITH A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE. Adjusted net profit Dh2.46bn, up 34% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. The company estimates around Dh1.5bn of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah, most of it in 2026, and guided cast metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 with the smelter at 25% of its reduction cells as of 26-Aug-2026 (315 of 1,262). THE COMPOSITION IS A PUBLIC CONFIRMATION OF THE MARGIN STRUCTURE THIS BOARD HAS DESCRIBED ALL CYCLE. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. The read-across to the alumina panel is direct - if Alunorte's 50% rate ends up lifting seaborne alumina, this is the margin that compresses first across the Gulf fleet.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL, DUE 13:20 LONDON, AND IT IS THE FIRST TEST OF THIS PAGE'S LEAD FINDING IN FOUR CALENDAR DAYS. The question is not the flat price, it is the STRUCTURE. Friday's session cut flat price 2.06% and left the backwardation at $24.00 against $25.00. A SESSION IN WHICH THE FRONT STAYS FIRM WOULD CONFIRM THE SELL-OFF WAS FINANCIAL AND UNRATIFIED BY THE PHYSICAL MARKET; a flattening or flipping spread, or a material warehouse inflow, would say the opposite and would invalidate this page's lead finding outright. NOTE THE TRAP CREATED BY OVERNIGHT NEWS: a Gulf-risk bid could lift the flat price while the spread flattens, which would look bullish and read bearish. WATCH THE SPREAD AND THE STOCK LINE BEFORE THE PRINT.

THE US 50% TARIFF ON ABOUT 100 CATEGORIES OF CANADIAN PRODUCTS TAKES EFFECT, with a ban on certain Canadian motor vehicles and dairy products following on 29-SEPTEMBER, against Canadian counter-tariffs already in force since 08-September at 50% across $27.6bn of imports. WHETHER ALUMINIUM SITS INSIDE THOSE 100 CATEGORIES IS NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED IN THE SOURCE AND IS NOT ASSUMED HERE - which is itself the reason to watch the day rather than to pre-position around it.

US FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION - THE LARGEST SINGLE SCHEDULED EVENT IN FRONT OF THIS MARKET, NOW TWO DAYS OUT. The 11-September session was the market beginning to price it: August core consumer prices landed a tenth above forecast at +0.3% month on month, the dollar firmed, and the entire metals board fell in one session. THE DOLLAR INDEX IS FIRMER AGAIN AT 99.33 AND THE REFERENCE PUBLISHER'S OWN HEADLINE READS THAT COPPER IS EXTENDING ITS FALL ON HAWKISH FED BETS. This event acts on aluminium through the dollar and through the discount rate applied to inventory financing, NOT through anything physical, which is why it can move the price without touching the curve.

RESTART OR CONTINUED CLOSURE OF THE SAUDI EAST-WEST CRUDE PIPELINE, AND THE RESCHEDULING OF THE POSTPONED IRAN-GULF HORMUZ CORRIDOR TALKS. These are now the two highest-asymmetry items on the page and they point the same way. The pipeline carries around 7 million barrels a day to Red Sea ports and is the principal Hormuz bypass; it was suspended after Thursday's drone attacks with no restart date. The corridor talks were postponed per Oman's Foreign Minister, with Saudi concerns reported and Bahrain out. A RESTART PLUS A RESCHEDULED MEETING WOULD UNWIND MOST OF THE OVERNIGHT ENERGY MOVE AND WITH IT THE GULF SUPPLY-RISK PREMIUM; CONTINUED CLOSURE WITH NO MEETING DATE WOULD DO THE OPPOSITE. This page will move the geopolitical trend on dated evidence in either direction, as it has now done twice in 48 hours.

RESOLUTION OF THE OCTOBER-DECEMBER ASIAN QUARTERLY PREMIUM. The pending range on this page is unchanged at $280-310 against a settled Q3 record of $395. It gained corroboration rather than movement: a second publisher on 12-September restated the $310-325/t producer offer as down 18-22% on Q3. THE NEWEST CONSENSUS OF $280-290 SITS BELOW THE PRODUCERS' OWN OFFER FLOOR, SO THE BURDEN OF CONCESSION IS ON THE SELLERS. A settlement at $285 would be a fall of roughly 28% in one quarter. A RENEWED GULF SUPPLY-RISK PREMIUM IS THE ONE THING THAT COULD FIRM THE OUTCOME, AND NO PUBLISHER HAS YET SAID IT HAS.

THE MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT CYCLE, NOW ABOUT THREE TO FOUR DAYS AWAY. Prebaked anode and coal tar pitch settle monthly around the 17th-18th, and green petcoke settles on its own cycle. The current Sep-26 anode mark of ~5,730 and the 13-August pitch mark of ~4,960 are the live figures until then. CARBON IS THE SECOND-LARGEST VARIABLE COST IN A SMELTER AFTER POWER, so this is the next scheduled movement in the input basket and the next scheduled append to the basket's trend histories - AND IT LANDS INTO A WEEK IN WHICH THE POWER LINE HAS ALREADY RISEN, WHICH IS WHY IT MATTERS MORE THIS MONTH THAN LAST.

WHETHER THE UPSTREAM LOOSENING SHOWS UP IN A DATED ALUMINA PRICE. The quantity evidence is unambiguous - Asian alumina exports up 27.36%, India's surplus quadrupled, Guinean bauxite shipments up 28.4% - but the most recent dated trade, $353.50/mt FOB East Australia on 11-September, was essentially flat on a five-week-old mark. IF THE NEXT DATED TRADE IS ALSO FLAT, THE SURPLUS IS BEING ABSORBED AND THE FALLING-COST THESIS IS WEAKER THAN THE VOLUME DATA SUGGESTS. That would be a genuine disconfirmation of a view this page has been building, and it is stated as a test rather than defended as a conclusion.

SLOVALCO'S GUIDED RESTART OF ITS FIRST 75,000 TONNES OF A 175,000-TONNE TOTAL, UNDER A SLOVAK CARBON-COST COMPENSATION AGREEMENT - NOW ROUGHLY TWO TO THREE WEEKS FROM ITS GUIDED WINDOW. It is the cleanest live test on this page of whether European smelting economics actually work at current power prices, AND THE POWER PRICE MOVED AGAINST IT OVERNIGHT: European gas +4.56% to about EUR 83.15/MWh, undoing yesterday's improvement. A SLIPPED OR CANCELLED RESTART WOULD BE A LOUDER SIGNAL THAN A COMPLETED ONE.

THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT - about fifteen weeks away and the largest scheduled structural event on this page's horizon. The European duty-unpaid premium is the row most directly exposed. Europe must replace those tonnes and both candidate sources deteriorated overnight: Gulf metal sits behind a chokepoint whose diplomatic path has been postponed and whose bypass is shut, and European restart capacity depends on power economics that have just turned the wrong way again. FIFTEEN WEEKS IS NOT LONG TO REROUTE A STRUCTURAL IMPORT FLOW.

risks.text: RE-ASSESSED 14-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP ON UNCHANGED EVIDENCE PLUS ONE DATED ESCALATION. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT TARIFF POLICY, NOT SUPPLY AND DEMAND, BECOMES THE DOMINANT DETERMINANT OF REGIONAL DELIVERED PRICE. The arithmetic demonstrated on Friday does not decay: Section 232 at 50% is levied on value, so at the carried cash of $3,274.00 the tariff leg of a US duty-paid tonne is $1,637.00 and the implied market leg against the unchanged $2,094/t assessment is $457.00. FRIDAY'S $69 FALL IN LONDON WIDENED THAT APPARENT MARKET LEG BY 8% WITH NOTHING PHYSICAL BEHIND IT. WHAT IS NEW IS DATED AND IMMINENT: the US 50% tariff on about 100 categories of Canadian products takes effect TOMORROW, 15-SEPTEMBER, with a vehicle and dairy import ban following on 29-SEPTEMBER, and Canada's 50% counter-tariffs have been in force since 08-September across $27.6bn of imports. WHETHER ALUMINIUM SITS INSIDE THOSE 100 CATEGORIES IS NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED AND IS NOT ASSUMED - but a regime escalating on a dated timetable is more likely to move than less.

RE-ASSESSED 14-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP, BUT WITH ONE SUPPORT WEAKENED AND THE WEAKENING STATED. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT CURTAILED AND DISRUPTED CAPACITY RETURNS FASTER THAN THE MARKET EXPECTS. The 11-September market review stating that ex-China resumptions continued and that damaged Middle Eastern capacity recovered is carried forward, with its evidential weight still capped because it is commentary rather than company disclosure. THE PIPELINE BEHIND IT IS UNCHANGED AND STILL DATED - NALCO licensing EGA's DX+ Ultra for a proposed 500,000 t/y Angul expansion, Rio Tinto acquiring Aurukun at up to 8 Mdt/y of bauxite, Rusal planning an Indonesian complex, Ashapura targeting 15 Mt/y of Guinean bauxite by FY28 - and none of it lands in 2026. WHAT CUTS AGAINST THIS ROW TODAY IS THE POWER PRICE: European gas +4.56% and US natural gas +2.06% make every marginal restart decision harder, not easier, and the European restart pipeline is the part of this risk most exposed to it. THE TREND IS HELD RATHER THAN LOWERED BECAUSE ONE SESSION OF DEARER GAS IS NOT A RESTART CANCELLATION, ON THE SAME LOGIC BY WHICH ONE SESSION OF CHEAPER GAS WAS REFUSED AS A RESTART CONFIRMATION YESTERDAY.

RE-ASSESSED 14-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP, AND THE EVENT THAT DECIDES IT IS NOW TWO DAYS AWAY. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT MACRO TIGHTENING OVERWHELMS THE MICRO TIGHTNESS. The 11-September session converted this from forecast to realised: US August core consumer prices landed a tenth above forecast at +0.3% month on month, the dollar firmed, and EVERY METAL ON THE BOARD FELL - zinc -2.27%, nickel -2.06%, aluminium -2.05%, copper -0.96%, lead -0.29%. THE DOLLAR INDEX IS FIRMER AGAIN AT 99.33 AND THE POSITIONING READ IS NO LONGER AN INFERENCE: the reference publisher's own dated metals headline this morning reads that copper is extending its fall on HAWKISH FED BETS. A DEARER-ENERGY, FIRMER-DOLLAR COMBINATION IS THE MOST ADVERSE SETTING FOR A DOLLAR-PRICED, ENERGY-INTENSIVE METAL, AND BOTH LEGS MOVED THAT WAY OVERNIGHT. This risk is kept separate from the aluminium-specific rows because it moves the whole complex at once and is therefore not diversifiable within metals.

RE-ASSESSED 14-SEPTEMBER. RAISED BACK FROM DOWN TO UP, REVERSING YESTERDAY'S DOWNGRADE, AND THIS IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL TREND CHANGE ON THIS PAGE THIS RUN. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS GEOPOLITICAL ESCALATION AROUND GULF SUPPLY AND ITS ROUTES. THE REASONING IS SET OUT IN FULL BECAUSE THIS ROW MOVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS IN 24 HOURS AND THAT DEMANDS AN EXPLANATION RATHER THAN AN ASSERTION. Yesterday it was lowered on dated 07-September reporting that Iran described an Oman arrangement as days away, with a temporary route reported agreed on 26-August. NEWER DATED EVIDENCE HAS OVERTAKEN THAT: talks between Iran and several Gulf nations on establishing a temporary shipping corridor through the Strait have been POSTPONED, stated publicly by Oman's Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi, with Saudi concerns over the proposal reported and Bahrain declining to participate, and the United States and Iran still at an impasse over control of the waterway. AND A SECOND, PHYSICAL ITEM ARRIVED WITH IT: Saudi Arabia has suspended its East-West crude pipeline after Thursday's drone attacks with no restart date - around 7 million barrels a day of capacity to Red Sea ports and the PRINCIPAL ROUTE THAT BYPASSES THE STRAIT. LOSING THE BYPASS IS WHAT MAKES THIS AN UPGRADE RATHER THAN A REVERSION: the hedge against the chokepoint is down at the same moment the diplomatic route to reopening the chokepoint is postponed. THE EARLIER REPORTING IS NOT DELETED AND WAS NOT WRONG - IT IS SUPERSEDED. Brent at a four-month high is the market's own vote on this row.

RE-ASSESSED 14-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT DOWN, AND THE HOLD IS DEFENDED RATHER THAN ASSUMED BECAUSE TODAY'S ENERGY MOVE MIGHT LOOK LIKE A REASON TO RAISE IT. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS SPECIFICALLY AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK PROPAGATING INTO SMELTER MARGIN - IT IS AN ORE AND REFINERY RISK, NOT A POWER RISK, AND THE TWO ARE NOT NETTED TOGETHER HERE. The alumina and bauxite evidence is unchanged and still points away from a shock in four separate series, all dated 12-September: Guinean bauxite shipments 4.33 Mt in the 21-27 August week, up 28.4% year on year; 2026 Guinea FOB forecast $34-46/dmt against $40-65/dmt in 2025; Australian FOB $39.15/wmt in FY26 against $51.48/wmt in FY25; Asian alumina exports 7.05 Mt in H1-2026, up 27.36% year on year; India's alumina trade surplus 1.72 Mt, nearly quadruple a year earlier. THE MOST RECENT DATED ALUMINA TRADE, 50,000 mt AT $353.50/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA ON 11-SEPTEMBER, IS ESSENTIALLY FLAT ON A FIVE-WEEK-OLD MARK - TONNES MOVING WITHOUT PRICES MOVING IS WHAT SURPLUS LOOKS LIKE. THE CONTRARY EVIDENCE IS KEPT VISIBLE AND IS WHY THE IMPACT RATING STAYS HIGH: Chinese ten-port bauxite inventories fell 1,610,000 tonnes week on week in the 11-September survey, thinning the buffer against a Guinea interruption, and Alunorte runs at full capacity only on an agreement publicly described as temporary - a gas-supply agreement, which today's energy move makes marginally more fragile.

RE-ASSESSED 14-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT FLAT ON NO NEW DATED INPUT, AND IT REMAINS THE MOST GENUINELY TWO-SIDED JUDGEMENT ON THIS PAGE. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT REGIONAL PREMIA RESET SHARPLY LOWER AND DRAG REALISED DELIVERED VALUES WITH THEM. Nothing newer than the 12-September corroboration has printed, so the pending Q4 Japanese range stays at $280-310 and is NOT tightened on a repeated reading: a second publisher restated the $310-325/t producer offer for October-December as down 18-22% on the $395/t Q3 settlement, which raises confidence in the upper bound without moving it. A settlement near the $280-290 consensus would be a fall of roughly 28% in a single quarter. ONE NEW CONSIDERATION IS RECORDED WITHOUT MOVING THE TREND: a renewed Gulf supply-risk premium and dearer freight risk argue for firmer rather than softer Asian and European premia at the margin, but a negotiation that is already inside its offer window is not usually reopened by a fortnight of geopolitics, and no publisher has said it has been.

RE-ASSESSED 14-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT DOWN. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT THE INVENTORY ARGUMENT UNDERPINNING THE BULL CASE STOPS WORKING. The last published warehouse line drew 250 tonnes to 244,100, a FIFTH consecutive decline, and it did so on a session in which flat price fell 2.06%. METAL DID NOT COME BACK TO THE WAREHOUSE ON A SHARPLY LOWER PRICE, which is the opposite of what a failing inventory argument looks like. NO NEW WAREHOUSE REPORT EXISTS YET TODAY AND NONE HAS BEEN ESTIMATED, so the risk is held rather than lowered further - a carried series is not a confirming one, and this is now the fourth calendar day without a fresh line. The stock axis has been re-checked this run and continues to bracket the series with roughly 9,100 tonnes of headroom to the floor.

RE-ASSESSED 14-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT DOWN, WITH THE SAME DELIBERATE NOTE THAT THE EVIDENCE IS AGEING RATHER THAN ACCUMULATING. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT THE CURVE SIGNAL IS TOO SMALL OR TOO FRAGILE TO ACT ON IN EITHER DIRECTION. It was lowered on 12-September because the signal had been tested in the harshest available way and held: flat price fell 2.06% and the backwardation narrowed by ONE DOLLAR, from $25.00 to $24.00, while stocks drew again. THAT TEST STANDS AND IS NOT RE-EARNED BY THE PASSAGE OF TIME. THE SIGNAL HAS NOW GONE FOUR CALENDAR DAYS WITHOUT A FURTHER TEST, WHICH IS WHY IT IS NOT LOWERED FURTHER. Today at 13:20 London is the test, and a flattening or flipping spread would reverse this row immediately. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY CREATED BY OVERNIGHT NEWS: a firmer flat price on a Gulf supply-risk bid would NOT by itself confirm the signal, because the signal is about structure rather than level - watch the spread, not the print.

RE-ASSESSED 14-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP AND REINFORCED BY THE POWER MOVE. THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT ON 31-DECEMBER-2026, ABOUT FIFTEEN WEEKS AWAY, AND IT IS THE LARGEST SCHEDULED STRUCTURAL EVENT ON THIS PAGE'S HORIZON. Europe must replace those tonnes from somewhere and both candidate sources deteriorated overnight: Gulf metal sits behind a chokepoint whose diplomatic resolution has just been postponed and whose bypass pipeline is shut, and European restart capacity depends on power economics that just moved the wrong way - European gas +4.56% to about EUR 83.15/MWh, undoing the improvement this page recorded yesterday. THAT IS THE VARIABLE SLOVALCO'S GUIDED Q4 RESTART OF ITS FIRST 75,000 TONNES IS MOST EXPOSED TO, roughly two to three weeks from its guided window. A SINGLE WEEK OF DEARER GAS DOES NOT CANCEL A RESTART ANY MORE THAN A SINGLE WEEK OF CHEAPER GAS UNDERWROTE ONE, BUT THE DIRECTION OF TRAVEL IS NOW AGAINST THE PIPELINE RATHER THAN FOR IT.

RE-ASSESSED 14-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT DOWN FOR A SECOND DAY, AND NOT CLEARED. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS SOURCE-DATA INTEGRITY: that the published price feed this page depends on is stale, cached or internally inconsistent without saying so. It was raised on 12-September when the German overview carried the 11-September board and the English overview still showed 10-September, and lowered on 13-September when both agreed. BOTH WERE RE-REQUESTED CACHE-BUSTED AGAIN THIS MORNING AND BOTH STILL CARRY 11-SEPTEMBER IDENTICALLY, WITH THE PER-METAL DAILY TABLE CONFIRMING NO LATER ROW EXISTS. TWO CONSECUTIVE CLEAN CROSS-CHECKS LOWER THE RISK; THEY DO NOT CLEAR IT, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS: the same source has lagged in BOTH languages within six weeks - English on 04-August, German on 12-September - so the cross-check remains mandatory every run and the per-metal daily tables remain the arbiter. ONE FURTHER STALENESS FINDING IS RECORDED TODAY RATHER THAN IGNORED: on the off-exchange reference board, thermal coal is stamped 11-September and the aluminium contract still reads 11-September at 0.00%, so parts of that board are three days stale while others refreshed to 14-September. A MIXED-VINTAGE BOARD IS A REAL HAZARD AND EVERY ROW TAKEN FROM IT CARRIES ITS OWN DATE STAMP ON THIS PAGE.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND THE 11-SEPTEMBER DATA SHARPENS THE CENTRAL PUZZLE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT: global primary production was reported down 1.7% year on year at 6.16 million tonnes and GCC output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000 - a genuine, large supply loss. YET China's August exports were 626,000 tonnes, taking January-August to 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year, and dated commentary describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE with Asian premiums collapsing toward a $280-290 Q4 consensus. A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
